name: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT)
summary: Transferring stool from a screened donor to restore a healthier gut microbial community.

name: Probiotics
summary: Live microorganisms given to confer a health benefit.

name: Prebiotics
summary: Substrates that are selectively used by host microorganisms.

name: Dietary fiber
summary: Diet-based interventions that change what gut microbes have available to ferment.

name: Recurrent C. difficile infection
summary: C. difficile infection that returns after treatment.

name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
summary: A common disorder of gut-brain interaction with abdominal pain and altered bowel habits.

name: Ulcerative colitis
summary: A form of inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colon.

name: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea
summary: Diarrhea that develops during or after a course of antibiotics.

name: Short-chain fatty acids
summary: Metabolites produced when gut bacteria ferment fiber.

name: Microbial diversity
summary: The number and balance of different microbes in the gut.

name: Bile acids
summary: Digestive molecules that gut microbes modify.

name: Type 2 diabetes
summary: A long-term condition in which blood sugar stays too high because the body doesn't use insulin well.

name: Bifidobacterium
summary: A group of gut bacteria generally considered beneficial, and a common ingredient in probiotics.

name: Prevotella
summary: A group of gut bacteria that tends to become more common with fiber-rich, plant-based diets.

name: Sulfate-reducing bacteria
summary: Gut bacteria such as Bilophila and Desulfovibrio that have been linked to inflammation.
